title: Oil
description: A small study in thick oil paint under a raking light: the word oil in ultramarine over pale yellow. Drag a flat sixteen-bristle brush through it and the paint smears, mixes like real pigment and piles into ridges that catch the gloss; four tubes are the only controls.
intent: One material, done properly: paint is stored as pigment plus height, the brush drags and deposits both, and the light does the rest. The gloss ridges along each bristle are the whole illusion.

sources.name: David Li, Fluid Paint (MIT)
sources.took: Ported the painting shader from shaders/painting.frag: the RYB trilinear colour cube, Sobel height normal, GGX specular with Smith shadowing and Schlick Fresnel, and the roughness, F0, diffuse and specular constants from paint.js; capsule splats between previous and current bristle positions from shaders/splat.frag and splat.vert. The fluid advection and bristle physics are replaced by a damped flat brush that smears paint within its footprint.

sources.name: darkroom.engineering, Lenis (MIT)
sources.took: Frame-rate independent damp for the brush tip and its turning
